Washington, June 1. Establishment of a new world seaplane altitude record by Lieutenant Apollo Soucek of the Navy in his attempt Tuesday was announced today by the National Aeronautic Association, after a check of his barograph by the Bureau of Standards.

Soucek exceeded by 50 feet the record of 1895 made by Lieut. G. G. Champion of the Navy in the same Wright Apache plane two years ago.

Soucek recently set a new altitude record for land planes, attaining a height of 1914 feet, but the honor was short-lived, as a few days later a German flyer, Willy Neunhofer, pushed his plane upward to a new world record of 12,123 feet.

The naval flyer set the new record for seaplanes on June 1, taking off at the naval air station here.
